intro: This repo is the Greenstand map tile server (`treetracker-map-tile-server` in `package.json`). It is a fork of node-mapnik, the Node.js bindings to Mapnik. The `greenstand/` directory holds the tile server; the rest is the node-mapnik addon. The addon needs the Mapnik libraries, so build and run it in Docker, as CI does.
prerequisites: Docker. The Dockerfile starts from the `dadiorchen/tile2:first` image, which holds the Mapnik libraries, and installs Node.js 14.
A PostgreSQL database with Treetracker data, to serve map tiles. The repo does not include one.

steps.title: Build the image
steps.text: The build compiles the addon with `make release_base`. CI builds the same Dockerfile.

steps.title: Run the tests
steps.text: At this commit, 3 of the 3,237 test assertions fail: one in `test/fonts.test.js` and two in `test/vector-tile.query.test.js`.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.text: Set `DB_URL` first: the full `postgresql://` URL of a database with Treetracker data, with the user, the password, the host, the port, and the database name. The other settings come from the committed `.env` file. The server listens on port 23300: http://localhost:23300/ shows a welcome line, and http://localhost:23300/viewer/ shows a map viewer. Tile requests (`/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`) need the Treetracker tables. With an empty database, the server logs `relation "active_tree_region" does not exist`, and the request gets no answer.
